title: Executive Team weekly
summary: Weekly operational meeting of the Executive Team: Copilot go-live dates, the overdue progress review backlog, the split of the eight new coach posts, P3 month-end, Northgrid and an all-staff town hall.
description: Weekly operational meeting of the Delcorn Executive Team (Mondays 09:30–10:30). Action log is kept by the Board Secretary.
agenda: Finance — P3 month-end and Meridian Q1 update

transcript.text: Morning everyone. Let's give it a minute — Priya's just messaged to say she's on her way back from the school run. Two minutes, she says.
Morning. I've put the action log in the chat. Three items carried over from last week, all on today's agenda anyway.
Morning. Can everyone hear me okay? My headset's been playing up all weekend.
Loud and clear, David. Right, let's start with Copilot, because that's the big one this week. Aisha?

Thanks, Helena. So, as you all saw on Friday, it's a go. Wave 1 — central teams plus the delivery managers — on Monday the ninth. Wave 2, coaches and tutors, on Monday the twenty-third. Wave 1 licences get assigned in batches from Thursday, and only to people who've finished Copilot Essentials.
Where are we on Essentials?
Seventy-one per cent of Wave 1 as of Friday. Ellie's chasing the rest. If someone hasn't done it by Monday they simply don't get a licence until they have.
I'll back that up in the managers' briefing. No exceptions — including this group.
Fair. Including me, I suspect. I've done about half of it.

There's one loose end on the salary file, PR-014. The org-wide link's gone and access is locked down to Marcus, Amy and Priya, but the label still needs upgrading to Highly Confidential, and only the owner can do that.
That's me. Sorry — I was in Leeds all of Friday. I'll do it today.
Sorry, sorry, I'm here. Have I missed anything about money?
Not yet, Priya — perfect timing. We're just finishing Copilot. Aisha, anything else?
Only that the service desk is extending hours on the ninth and tenth, eight till six. That's it from me.
Great. David — reviews.

Yes. So Rachel's note this morning has {{fact:overdue_reviews}} learners with an overdue progress review. That's the highest it's been all year, and with the funding audit sample due in December it's a genuine exposure.
And it's QIP-07, which is already Red. If an inspector pulled a sample tomorrow, that's the first thing they'd find.

Agreed. Rachel's asked Sam and Laura for recovery plans by Wednesday — all the Red learners re-booked by this Friday, the sixth, and everything else by Friday the twenty-seventh. I'll bring the trajectory back here next Monday.
Is the twenty-seventh realistic?
It's tight. Honestly it depends on caseload relief, which is really Marcus's item.
Let's go straight to that, then. Marcus.

So, the eight additional coach posts the board approved. Adverts went live on Thursday and Joe's had forty-odd applications for the Data role already. The question for this group is the split by academy.
Data's the hottest, no question. Leadership after that — Kwame's carrying thirty.
Can I make a case for AI? If the Valemont cohort lands we'll need AI4 capacity in January.
My proposal is four Data, three Leadership and one AI — and we revisit the AI number if Valemont signs.
Everyone comfortable with that? ... Okay. Agreed — four, three, one.
And I'd like first interviews before Christmas. Joe's aiming for panels in the week of the sixteenth.

Just flagging that the part-year cost — the hundred and eighty-six thousand — isn't in the budget phasing yet, so it'll show as an adverse cost variance from December. That's expected, not a surprise.
Noted. Priya, while you've got the floor.

Month-end. P3 close is under way. Early sight is that October funding is behind budget again, mostly in the Data Academy, but I'm not quoting a number until Andrew and Nicole have split timing from structural. I'll have that by Wednesday and I'll sign off the R03 return on Thursday.
And Meridian? Richard wants his update by Friday.
I'll draft it once the variance is understood. I want to be careful how we describe the year to date.
You've got the pipeline headline from me already.
Thanks. Tom, anything else commercial?
Two things. Northgrid — Marion Ackroyd, their Chief Digital Officer, has agreed to meet us. Thursday the nineteenth of November at their Coventry office. Helena, I'd really like you there.
It's in the diary. Who else?
Ravi, and Ben for the AI curriculum conversation. Second thing — Kestrel have paused new starts while they restructure. No losses yet, but I'm watching it.
Kestrel have forty-odd on programme. Can we make sure the coaches hear it from us before the learners hear rumours?
Lewis is speaking to their Early Careers Manager this week. I'll get him to brief the coaches.
Siân?

Quick one. The Q1 OTJ audit is final. No ineligible claims, but seven behind-plan learners have no catch-up plan in their latest review, so that finding's rated High and QIP-06 stays Red. Sam's putting plans in place for those seven by the fourteenth.
And Grace asked me to say all {{fact:open_safeguarding}} open cases are within response standards.

Thank you. AOB — Birmingham opens on the sixteenth, coffee morning at ten, and I'll be there. I'd also like an all-staff town hall before Wave 2 — partly Copilot, partly Q1. Thursday the twelfth at lunchtime?
That works. It's not an ILR week.
I'll send the invite on your behalf this week, Helena, and collect questions in advance through a form.
Lovely. Oliver, can you read the actions back?

Marcus — label on the salary file today. David — review trajectory next Monday. Marcus — confirm the four-three-one split with Joe and book panels for the week of the sixteenth, by Friday. Priya — variance split and R03 sign-off by Thursday, Meridian update by Friday. Me — town hall invite by Wednesday. Tom — Lewis to brief the Kestrel coaches.
Perfect. Thanks all — same time next week.

recap.summary: The Executive Team confirmed Copilot go-live dates (Wave 1 Monday 9 November, Wave 2 Monday 23 November) and that licences will only be assigned after Copilot Essentials. David Okafor reported {{fact:overdue_reviews}} overdue progress reviews and a recovery plan due mid-week. The team agreed how to split the eight new skills coach posts (four Data, three Leadership, one AI). Priya Raman gave an early view that October funding is behind budget and will report the timing/structural split by Wednesday. Tom Whitfield confirmed a meeting with Northgrid's Chief Digital Officer on 19 November, and Helena Marsh asked for an all-staff town hall on 12 November.

topics.title: Copilot rollout — Wave 1 readiness
topics.text: Wave 1 (central teams and delivery managers) goes live on 9 November and Wave 2 (coaches and tutors) on 23 November. 71% of Wave 1 had completed Copilot Essentials on Friday; no licence without completion. PR-014 (salary benchmarking file) is remediated apart from the Highly Confidential label, which Marcus Bell will apply.

topics.title: Overdue progress reviews
topics.text: {{fact:overdue_reviews}} learners have an overdue review — the highest this year — and QIP-07 is Red. Delivery managers are submitting plans: Red learners re-booked by 6 November, everything else by 27 November. Delivery depends on caseload relief.

topics.title: Additional skills coach posts
topics.text: Adverts for the eight board-approved posts went live last Thursday. Agreed split: four Data, three Leadership, one AI, to be revisited if the Valemont cohort is signed. Interview panels planned for the week of 16 November. The £186,000 part-year cost is not yet phased in the budget.

topics.title: Finance — P3 month-end
topics.text: October funding is behind budget again, mainly in the Data Academy. The CFO will split timing from structural variance by Wednesday, sign off R03 on Thursday and send the Q1 trading update to Meridian by Friday.

topics.title: Commercial, quality and AOB
topics.text: Northgrid's CDO meeting is booked for 19 November in Coventry (Helena Marsh, Tom Whitfield, Ravi Sharma, Dr Ben Hartley). Kestrel Logistics has paused new starts. The Q1 OTJ audit is final with a High finding on catch-up plans. Birmingham hub opens 16 November; an all-staff town hall will be held on 12 November.

decisions: Copilot go-live dates confirmed: Wave 1 on 9 November, Wave 2 on 23 November 2026; no licence without Copilot Essentials, no exceptions.
The eight additional skills coach posts are split four Data, three Leadership and one AI, to be revisited if the Valemont cohort is signed.
An all-staff town hall will be held on Thursday 12 November at lunchtime.

Bring the overdue progress review recovery trajectory to the Executive Team

Report the October funding variance split (timing vs structural) and sign off the R03 return

title: Overdue progress reviews — recovery plan
summary: Delivery leadership turn the approved overdue-review recovery plans into owners and dates: Red re-bookings, caseload moves, Aptiva reminders, a daily Power BI tile and a weekly check-in.
description: Follow-up to Rachel's email 'Overdue progress reviews – action needed this week'. Please bring your overdue numbers by coach.
agenda: Funding audit sample and OTJ catch-up plans
trainer_notes: DELIBERATE TEACHING FLAW. The intelligent recap contains two errors against the transcript: (1) the action to move five TL3 learners from Kwame Mensah to Chloe Davies is assigned to Sam Patel (P012) — in the transcript Sam offers, but Laura Chen (P013) declines and keeps it, and Rachel confirms 'Laura owns that, Friday the sixth'; (2) Kate Simmons' daily overdue tile is shown as due 16 November — in the transcript Kate first muddles the day but then confirms Monday 9 November. All other actions are correct. Used in scenario S-MTG-02.

transcript.text: Hi both — and hi, Isabel. Kate's said she'll be five minutes late, she's in the Aptiva release call. Let's crack on.
Afternoon.
Hi Rachel.
Laura, I think you're on mute.
Sorry — how about now? New headset. It mutes itself if I so much as breathe on it.

Got you. Right — thank you both for the plans, they were exactly what I needed and I approved them at lunchtime. I want to use this half hour to turn them into who's doing what by when, because I'm updating David on Monday.
Headline first. This morning's extract says {{fact:overdue_reviews}} overdue. Sam — AI, Data and Digital?

Data's {{fact:dlv_data_overdue}}, AI {{sql:SELECT SUM(overdue_reviews) FROM coach_caseloads WHERE academy='AI Academy'}} and Digital {{sql:SELECT SUM(overdue_reviews) FROM coach_caseloads WHERE academy='Digital Academy'}}. The Reds are the priority — we're now at about eighty-five per cent of Red reviews in diaries, up from seventy on Tuesday.
And the rest by Friday?
Every Red booked by Friday, yes. Held by Friday is a different question — a few employers just can't do this week.
Booked with a date is fine for the Reds, as long as it's within ten working days. Laura?

Leadership's {{sql:SELECT SUM(overdue_reviews) FROM coach_caseloads WHERE academy='Leadership Academy'}} and People {{sql:SELECT SUM(overdue_reviews) FROM coach_caseloads WHERE academy='People Academy'}}. Same story as my email — about a third were booked and then cancelled by the line manager.
Are we using the mentor rule yet?
From this week, yes. After two cancellations the coach can hold it with the nominated workplace mentor, and we still get the employer to sign it off.
Good. Caseload moves. Sam, the DA4 starters.
Twelve DA4 starters moving from the two busiest coaches to our September joiners. I'll do the reassignment in Aptiva myself tomorrow, so it's clean for Monday's report.
Lovely. And Fatima plus two senior coaches picking up ten reviews each?
Yep. Fatima's already started. I'll send you the names of the other two by tomorrow.
Laura — Kwame.
So, five TL3 learners from Kwame to Chloe. Chloe's on twenty-two and she's happy to take them. I'll make the change in Aptiva and let both employers know. Done by Friday.
Do you want me to do those with my DA4 batch? I'm in there anyway.
No, honestly, it's fine — I need to speak to the line managers anyway, so I'll do it. Thanks though.
Okay — Laura owns that, Friday the sixth. Isabel, will Monday's caseload report pick up both moves?
As long as they're in Aptiva by five o'clock on Friday, yes. I'll also re-send the first-review-due list, because a few of the moved learners are new starters and their eight-week clock is ticking.
Please do.
Hi — sorry, sorry, the release call overran. Have I missed my bit?
Perfect timing, Kate. Two things: the day-seventy reminder from the team meeting, and I want a daily number.
So the day-seventy reminder — the automated Aptiva nudge to the coach when it's seventy days since the last review — is built and in test. Still on track for the thirteenth.
And daily tracking?
I can add a daily overdue tile to the Power BI caseload report, by academy and by coach. I can have it ready by Monday — not this Monday, obviously, I mean... Monday the sixteenth? No, hang on.
Kate, today's Wednesday. This coming Monday is the ninth.
Ha — yes, sorry, my days have completely gone. Monday the ninth. It'll be ready for your meeting with David.
Brilliant, thank you.
Kate, while you're here — the OTJ showing zero after a programme transfer. Is that fixed for good? James had another one yesterday.
It's fixed for new transfers. His might be an old one. Send me the learner ID — not the name — and I'll check.
Will do.
Employers. Laura, you mentioned three employers who cancel the most.
Yes. I'll ask the client partners to nudge them — Sophie has two of them and Ravi has one.
Can you get that done by Friday as well?
Monday, realistically. Sophie's at Halden Valley tomorrow and Friday.
Monday the ninth, then.

Last thing — the funding audit sample in December. Daniel's reminded me that any sampled learner with an overdue review is an evidence gap. Sam, the seven from the OTJ audit without catch-up plans — those are yours by the fourteenth?
Yes, Daniel sent me the IDs. Four are done already.
Great. I'd like us to meet weekly on this until we're under a hundred. Wednesdays at two, thirty minutes. Isabel and Kate, you too. I'll send a series out.
Can we make the target 'under a hundred by the twenty-seventh'? Otherwise it never ends.
Yes, let's make that explicit. Under a hundred by Friday the twenty-seventh, and everything else re-booked by then.
One more thing — I've been using Copilot in Excel on the caseload report to rank coaches by overdue reviews and Reds. Once we're licensed on Monday I'll share the prompt.
Please do. Okay, I'll trust the recap for the actions. Thanks, all.
Bye!

recap.summary: Rachel Moss and the delivery managers turned the approved recovery plans for the {{fact:overdue_reviews}} overdue progress reviews into owners and dates. Red learners will all be booked by Friday 6 November, caseloads will be rebalanced (12 DA4 starters and five TL3 learners), Kate Simmons will add automated reminders and a daily Power BI tile, and the team will meet weekly until overdue reviews are under 100, targeted for 27 November.

About 85% of Red reviews are now in diaries. Around a third of Leadership and People overdue reviews were cancelled by line managers; the nominated-mentor rule applies after two cancellations.

title: P3 month-end review — October funding variance
summary: CFO-led review of the October 2026 (P3) close: the funding variance by academy, timing versus structural, R03 sign-off, the full-year forecast and downside scenario, and cost items.
description: Month-end review following the 'P3 month-end — October funding variance' email thread. Nicole to talk through the academy breakdown; Daniel for R03 validation.
agenda: October and YTD funding vs budget
Variance by academy — timing vs structural

transcript.text: Hi all. Thanks for making time — I know it's month-end and everyone's tired. Peter, are you with us?
Yes, sorry, camera off — I'm eating a very late lunch.
That's fine. Daniel's joining for the R03 bit. Nicole, can you walk us through what you sent this morning? I want it said out loud, not just sitting in an email.

Sure. October funding was {{fact:fin_oct_funding}} against a budget of seven hundred and ninety thousand, so thirty-seven thousand nine hundred and twenty short. Year to date we're at {{fact:fy27_ytd_funding}} against two million three hundred and thirty thousand — that's minus ninety-seven thousand two hundred and ten.
Second month running.

Yes. By academy, year to date: Data's the big one, minus eighty point eight k. Two reasons — the Northgrid Data Analyst cohort moved from October to January, and eleven completion payments slipped into November because EPA dates moved.
And the completion element of that is about thirty-five thousand?
Roughly thirty-five k, yes. That's timing — it comes back in November and December.
And the rest?

AI is minus twenty-four point eight k. Only ten starts in October against twenty-one last October — employers waited for the Level 4 launch pack. Digital minus twenty point three, People minus three point one, both just low starts on small numbers. Leadership is plus thirty-one point eight, because Operations Manager starts are soaking up the old Senior Leader demand.
So the Level 7 change is actually showing as a positive in Leadership.
In that academy, yes. It's a shift, not a gain overall.
So my split is about thirty-five k timing and about sixty-two k structural or at risk. Does everyone agree with that framing?
I'd be a bit careful calling all of the sixty-two structural. Some of the AI number comes back if Valemont lands in January.
Fair. Let's call it 'structural or at risk', and name Valemont as the swing factor.
That's how I've worded it in the commentary sheet.
Good. Please finish the variance commentary so it matches exactly what you've just said. By when?
Tomorrow, ten o'clock — before you sign R03.
Daniel — R03.
Hi. Validation's clean apart from two prior-learning warnings. I've checked both — the price reductions are applied correctly, so they're fine. Evidence is in the Funding and ILR folder.
Then I'll sign it off first thing tomorrow.
The data freeze was five o'clock yesterday, so nothing's changed since.
Andrew — forecast.
As you asked, I'm holding the full year at budget for now, and I'll add a downside scenario where January starts slip by twenty per cent.
When can I see it?
Monday the ninth. That gives us a day before the management accounts go to Meridian on the tenth.
Monday's fine. And build in the coach recruitment — the hundred and eighty-six thousand part-year — because that isn't phased in the budget.
Already on my list. I'll phase it from December.
Peter — costs.

Broadly on budget. Two things. Brightside — the overdue summit invoice — went out in today's payment run, so that's closed. And I've accrued for the Wellspring EAP usage, which came in higher in October after Wellbeing Week.
Trend or one-off?
Probably a one-off, but I'll keep an eye on it.
And the note to Marketing about POs? So we don't get another Brightside.
I'll send Jess a short note this week — changes on the day need a PO variation before the supplier invoices.
Please — by Friday.
Nicole, out of interest, how long did that breakdown take you?
About forty minutes. Honestly, most of it was looking up the budget phasing.
Once Copilot's switched on in Excel next week, that's exactly the sort of thing to try.

Mm — with checking. I don't want a number in a Meridian pack that nobody has traced back to the source. On Meridian: I'm sending Richard the Q1 update tomorrow morning, and Andrew, I'll want your downside scenario in the management accounts pack on the tenth.
Understood.
Okay. Thanks, everyone. Go home on time for once.

recap.summary: Nicole Brooks confirmed October 2026 funding of {{fact:fin_oct_funding}} against a £790,000 budget (−£37,920) and year-to-date funding of {{fact:fy27_ytd_funding}} against £2,330,000 (−£97,210). The variance was framed as about £35k timing (Data Academy completion payments) and about £62k structural or at risk, with the Valemont cohort as the swing factor. R03 validation is clean and will be signed off on 5 November. The full-year forecast is held at budget with a downside scenario of January starts slipping by 20%.

topics.title: October and YTD funding vs budget
topics.text: October −£37,920; YTD −£97,210. By academy YTD: Data −£80.8k (Northgrid Data Analyst cohort moved to January; 11 completion payments slipped to November), AI −£24.8k (10 October starts vs 21 last year), Digital −£20.3k, People −£3.1k, Leadership +£31.8k (Operations Manager starts absorbing former Senior Leader demand).

topics.title: Timing vs structural
topics.text: About £35k is timing and about £62k is 'structural or at risk'; part of the AI shortfall would reverse if the Valemont cohort starts in January.

topics.title: R03 return
topics.text: Validation clean apart from two prior-learning warnings, both checked by Daniel Evans. Data freeze was 3 November 17:00.

topics.title: Forecast and downside scenario
topics.text: Full year held at budget. Andrew Clarke will add a downside scenario (January starts −20%) and phase the £186,000 coach recruitment cost from December.

topics.title: Costs
topics.text: Brightside Events invoice paid in the 4 November payment run. Wellspring EAP usage accrued after Wellbeing Week. Marketing to be reminded that on-the-day changes need a PO variation.

decisions: Describe the YTD variance as about £35k timing and about £62k structural or at risk, naming the Valemont cohort as the swing factor.
Hold the full-year forecast at budget for now, with a downside scenario of January starts slipping by 20%.
R03 to be signed off by the CFO on the morning of 5 November.

actions.action: Finish the variance commentary sheet using the agreed timing/structural wording
Sign off the R03 ILR return
Add a downside scenario (January starts −20%) to the full-year forecast
Phase the £186,000 part-year coach recruitment cost into the forecast from December
Send Marketing a note on PO variations for on-the-day supplier changes
Send the Q1 trading update to Meridian Education Group

title: Copilot Wave 1 readiness stand-up
summary: Daily Copilot readiness stand-up: corrected go-live dates, Wave 1 licence group and training completion, service desk cover, and the outstanding label on the salary benchmarking file (PR-014).
description: Daily 30-minute stand-up for the Copilot rollout team until Wave 2 is live.

transcript.text: Morning! Quick one today — I've got a hard stop at quarter to.
Morning.
Morning all.
Ellie — we can see your lips moving but nothing's coming through.
Sorry! Wrong microphone. Can you hear me now?

Yes. Right — round the room, then the salary file. First, just so we're all saying the same thing, because the FAQ and the Champions chat still say the second and the sixteenth: the dates are Wave 1 on Monday the ninth and Wave 2 on Monday the twenty-third. The exec confirmed that on Friday.
I'll update the FAQ today. The known-issues page still says central teams were licensed on the second of November, which is now just wrong.
Please. Ellie, could you post a correction in the Champions channel?
Will do, this morning.

Licences: the Wave 1 group's built — sixty-eight people now we've added the delivery managers. Licences assign automatically when Essentials completion syncs over from the CPD portal, which runs overnight.
Completion, Ellie?

Seventy-eight per cent of Wave 1 as of this morning, up from seventy-one on Friday. Fifteen people outstanding. I'm sending personal reminders today, and if they still haven't done it I'll copy their line managers on Thursday.
Do it. Mohammed, service desk?

Extended hours, eight till six, on the ninth and tenth, with two of us on Copilot tickets. And the known issue — Copilot not showing in classic Outlook — the workaround's in the FAQ: switch to new Outlook.
Liam — PR-014.

So: link removed, inheritance broken, access is Marcus, Amy and Priya only, and Restricted Content Discovery is on for People, Safeguarding and Exec. The only thing outstanding is the label. It's still Confidential, it needs to be Highly Confidential, and because that label encrypts, Marcus has to apply it as the owner.
He told the exec yesterday he'd do it yesterday.
It was still Confidential at eight o'clock this morning. I checked.
I'll go and sit with him today — he's in London. It's five minutes in Excel.
I want PR-014 closed before Wave 1. Let's say end of Thursday, the fifth, at the latest. If it isn't, I'd rather take the file off the site entirely than delay anyone's licence.
Agreed. I'll close it in the permissions workbook the moment the label's on.

Related — the auto-labelling policy for salary and NI numbers. Since Thursday it's labelled a hundred and forty Ledgerline exports in Finance as Confidential. No false positives that I've seen, but Peter asked whether it'll catch payroll PDFs.
It should — it's content-based, not file-type. Kate, could you test it with a dummy payslip?
Yep, today.
Sorry — ignore the barking. Delivery driver.
Ha. Biscuit has opinions.
Kate, the permissions review generally?
All of last week's remediation is holding. I re-ran the oversharing report last night — no new 'Everyone' links. The only open Critical finding is PR-014.
And the incident?
DPI-2026-019 — logged, not reportable. Marcus's note to the twenty-three recipients went out on Friday, and the anonymised case study goes into the Responsible AI module before Wave 2.
Hi, sorry — only just seen the invite. Anything for comms?
Just the date correction, Jess. The FAQ and the Champions channel are being fixed.
The Hub article and the Digest both already say the ninth, so we're fine there. I'll add the town hall date once Oliver sends it.
Perfect. Same time tomorrow — thanks, all.

recap.summary: The rollout team aligned on the confirmed go-live dates (Wave 1 Monday 9 November, Wave 2 Monday 23 November) and agreed to correct the FAQ and Champions channel, which still show 2 and 16 November. The Wave 1 licence group has 68 people and 78% have completed Copilot Essentials. PR-014 (salary benchmarking file) is fully remediated except the Highly Confidential label, which the owner must apply; Aisha Karim set a deadline of end of Thursday 5 November.

title: Northgrid Energy — Quarterly Business Review Q1 2026/27
summary: Q1 2026/27 QBR with Northgrid Energy plc: progress RAG, field-operations OTJ, the Data Analyst cohort moving to January, EPA capacity, a Data Engineering cohort, the CDO's AI roadmap and Copilot Adoption Bootcamps.
description: Quarterly business review for August–October 2026. Ravi will share the QBR slides on screen.
agenda: Growth: Data Engineering, AI roadmap, Copilot Adoption Bootcamps

transcript.text: Morning Terence, morning Gareth — thanks for having us. Laura and Sam are both here, and Ryan's on as well.
Morning Ravi. Helen's going to join at about twenty past — she's coming out of a network ops meeting.
No problem at all. I'll share the deck. Can you see it?
We can see your desktop. And your inbox.
Ah — sorry. How about now?
Got it.

So, the quarter at a glance. You've got {{fact:ptn_northgrid_on_programme}} apprentices on programme with us, which keeps you our biggest partner. {{sql:SELECT COUNT(*) FROM learners WHERE employer_id='EMP1001' AND status IN ('Active','Break in learning','Gateway','EPA') AND progress_rag='Green'}} are Green, {{sql:SELECT COUNT(*) FROM learners WHERE employer_id='EMP1001' AND status IN ('Active','Break in learning','Gateway','EPA') AND progress_rag='Amber'}} Amber and {{sql:SELECT COUNT(*) FROM learners WHERE employer_id='EMP1001' AND status IN ('Active','Break in learning','Gateway','EPA') AND progress_rag='Red'}} Red.
The Reds — are those mostly field operations again?
Mostly, yes. Team Leaders on shift patterns. The common thread is off-the-job time — they just can't get it on a rotating shift.
That's exactly what I hear from the depots.
What would really help is agreeing protected learning time with two depot managers as a pilot — Nuneaton and Rugby. Two hours a fortnight, actually rostered.
I'll sponsor that. Gareth, can you get Laura in front of the depot managers?
Yes, I'll make the introductions this week.
Then I'll aim to have both depots agreed by the thirteenth of November.
Data Analyst cohort. Terence, I understand there's a change?
Yes, I'm afraid so. With the Network Analytics restructure, the line managers aren't confirmed yet. We'd like to move the October Data Analyst cohort to January. It's twelve starts.
That's fine from our side. Monday the eleventh of January works for induction.
The eleventh is good. I'll need to redo the commitments in the apprenticeship service, though.
I'll send you a revised start plan and the commitments checklist, Gareth. By Friday?
Perfect.
Just so you know, it does move some funding for us into the new year — but the most important thing is that they start with a manager who's bought in.
Appreciated, Ravi.

Can I raise EPA? You've got {{sql:SELECT COUNT(*) FROM learners WHERE employer_id='EMP1001' AND status IN ('Gateway','EPA')}} at gateway or in EPA, and a chunk of the Data Analysts all hit gateway in the next quarter. Assessor capacity gets tight in January.
What do you need from us?
Nothing yet — I just want to book Pinnacle slots early. I'll get provisional dates in by the sixth of November and share them with Gareth.
Sounds good.
While we wait for Helen — Terence, how are the line managers finding the new review sign-off in the employer portal?
Mixed, honestly. The ones who use it like it. The ones who don't, don't open the emails. That's a people problem, not a portal problem.
Hi, sorry — Helen Okoro, Network Analytics. Apologies, the ops meeting ran over.
Welcome, Helen! We were just talking about your team's cohort, actually.
Good timing, then. I wanted to talk about Data Engineering. I've got maybe eight people who'd suit it — but April, not before. Not until the restructure's settled.
April works well for us. Ryan, can we set up a discovery call with Helen for late November?
I'll send some times across by next Tuesday.

The other big thing. Marion — our Chief Digital Officer — has been asked by our board for an AI roadmap. She met Tom at the Skills Summit and she'd like a proper conversation about AI skills. And, to be frank, she's been approached by another provider.
Thank you for being straight with us. I'll get Tom and Helena to set that up — in person, at yours, if Marion prefers.
She would. Coventry. November, if you can.
Last one — the Copilot Adoption Bootcamps for the corporate centre. Six hundred people; we'd suggest six cohorts to start, at nine and a half thousand per cohort, so fifty-seven thousand.
Send me a proposal. If it's under sixty thousand I can sign it off without procurement going out to tender.
I'll have it with you by the end of next week — Friday the thirtieth.
Will it cover Copilot in Excel? Our finance team are desperate.
It can — each cohort's tailored. I'll put an Excel option in.

Let me play the actions back. Laura — protected time with Nuneaton and Rugby by the thirteenth of November, with Gareth's introductions. Ryan — revised January start plan to Gareth by Friday, and times for Helen's discovery call by Tuesday. Sam — provisional Pinnacle slots by the sixth of November. Me — the bootcamp proposal by the thirtieth, and I'll ask Tom and Helena to set up the meeting with Marion in Coventry this week.
That's right. Thanks, everyone — really useful.
I'll send the invite for the next QBR, end of January.

title: Inspection readiness review — autumn term
summary: Termly inspection readiness review: evidence map currency, QIP Reds (OTJ and overdue reviews), safeguarding, learner voice, Copilot guardrails for review judgements and a January mock deep dive.
description: Honest look at where we would be if the inspection call came on Monday. Papers: Inspection Readiness Evidence Map, QIP 2026/27 (October RAG), Q1 OTJ audit.

transcript.text: Afternoon, all. Rachel's going to be about ten minutes late, she's with a coach. Ben, are you there? I can see your initials but nothing else.
I'm here — the bandwidth in Bristol is terrible today, so camera off, sorry.
No problem. The purpose today is an honest look at where we'd be if the call came on Monday. We were Strong in February and I don't want any complacency. Hannah — evidence map.

So the evidence map has forty-eight items across the evaluation areas. Forty-one are current. Seven are out of date, and the biggest are two curriculum reviews — DE5 and SL7 — that are overdue in the review cycle.
Yes, they're mine. SL7 is awkward because of the Level 7 changes; we don't really know what that programme looks like next year. DE5 I can just get done.
When?
Both by the eleventh of December. SL7 might end up as a 'review and recommend', but it'll be done.
That's fine — a documented decision is evidence in itself.
QIP. We've got two Reds: QIP-06, OTJ time not protected, and QIP-07, overdue reviews.
On QIP-06 — the Q1 audit final report goes up this afternoon. F3 is High: seven of the twenty behind-plan learners had no catch-up plan in their latest review. Sam's on those for the fourteenth.
And the re-test?
F3 and F5 are both in the Q2 sample, fieldwork late January. Kate's also confirmed the KSB field in Aptiva can be made mandatory by mid-December.
Good. That's the kind of thing an inspector would want to see — not just that we found it, but that we checked the fix worked.
Hi — sorry, sorry. A coach in tears about her caseload; I couldn't leave it.
Of course, Rachel. Perfect timing — overdue reviews.

{{fact:overdue_reviews}} as of yesterday's extract. Plans from Sam and Laura come in tomorrow. Reds re-booked by Friday and everything else by the twenty-seventh. I'll be honest — the twenty-seventh is tight.
From an inspection point of view, what they'd also pick up is whether the reviews that do happen are any good. Targets are still the main development area in observations.
Which is QIP-04, and that one's Green. So the story is 'quality improving, timeliness not'. I can live with that for a month, not for a term.

Safeguarding: {{fact:open_safeguarding}} open or under monitoring, all within response standards. One new case last week through the coach route, triaged the same day. Prevent risk assessment unchanged.
Any themes?
Wellbeing and workload, as always — and a couple of learners mentioning money worries. I'd like coaches to have the cost-of-living signposting in the review template.
I can add that to the review template guidance when it next goes out.
Thank you.
Learner voice — NPS is {{fact:learner_nps_12m}} for the last twelve months. OTJ time is the top negative theme in the comments, which lines up nicely with Daniel's audit.
Can I go off-piste for a second? The AI3 learners are asking whether they can use Copilot in their portfolios. We need one answer, not five.

Good segue, Ben. Wave 2 brings coaches on from the twenty-third. I want it absolutely clear: Copilot does not write review judgements or EPA readiness decisions. It can draft a summary from a transcript; the coach owns the judgement. Learner use is a separate conversation for Curriculum Board.
It's in section five of the AUP, and Liam's put a slide in Copilot Essentials.
Good. Hannah, I'd like the observation framework to say the same thing — if an observer sees a Copilot draft, they check the coach has edited it and the targets are genuinely theirs.
I'll draft the wording for Quality Board.
Last item: a mock deep dive. I'd like to run one in January — two days, three deep dives: Data Academy, Leadership and safeguarding. Tuesday the nineteenth and Wednesday the twentieth of January.
That's not on top of the January ILR?
No — the January return's done the week before. The nineteenth is clear.
Then that's decided. Hannah leads it, and I'll ask Professor Qureshi whether he'd like to observe as link NED.
I'll have a plan together by the end of November.
Lovely. Anything else? ... No? Thanks, all — that was really useful.

recap.summary: Dr Siân Llewellyn led the autumn inspection readiness review. 41 of 48 evidence items are current; the main gaps are the overdue DE5 and SL7 curriculum reviews. QIP-06 (OTJ) and QIP-07 (overdue reviews) are Red, with {{fact:overdue_reviews}} overdue reviews and a High finding from the Q1 OTJ audit. Safeguarding cases ({{fact:open_safeguarding}}) are within standards and learner NPS is {{fact:learner_nps_12m}}. The group reaffirmed that Copilot must not write review judgements or EPA readiness decisions and agreed a mock deep dive on 19–20 January 2027.
